_description: Design-independent node/edge render contract for the canonical journey graph. Derived from the 7 node kinds actually present in src/canonical/types.ts and the edge shapes they produce — no invented node type. Colour, spacing, typography, pixel values: none. A design adapter maps this to real components.

trigger.presentIn: 255/255 journeys (exactly one per journey, always the entry)
invalidStates: evidence.requires is empty (validator rejects this — err trigger_no_evidence)
more than one trigger node in a journey (validator rejects — err trigger_count)
derivedDisplayMetadata: event humanized to a sentence-case label (see canonical-view.ts's humanEvent)
trigger.accessibilityLabelContract: Accessible name = the humanized event label, prefixed 'Journey starts when'. evidence.source is announced as a qualifier ('behavioral signal', 'authoritative fact', etc.) since it changes what the journey is allowed to conclude.

action.presentIn: 1131 nodes across all journeys (median 4-5 per journey)
requiredData: does (headline text — see content-stats: median 214, max 483 chars)
derivedDisplayMetadata: none — does is a headline with no secondary field, per the content-stats risk flag
action.accessibilityLabelContract: Accessible name = does, in full — this text cannot be safely summarized for a11y since it is the node's only content. writes entries are announced as 'records: {field}' where mode='append' is distinguished from mode='set' (append preserves history, set overwrites it — a meaningful distinction for anyone auditing the journey).

condition.presentIn: 702 nodes, 254/255 journeys (near-universal — not a distinguishing structural signal by itself)
requiredData: branches (>=2 items, each: label, when, to)
invalidStates: fewer than 2 branches (validator rejects — err single_branch)
a branch with an empty when (validator rejects — err branch_no_test)
derivedDisplayMetadata: branch.label is chip/pill-safe (median 13 chars); branch.when is NOT and must render as separate expandable detail
condition.accessibilityLabelContract: The condition node's accessible name is asks. Each branch edge announces as '{label}: {when}' so a screen-reader user gets the decision criterion, not just an arbitrary letter.

invalidStates: timeout.after is empty (validator rejects — a wait with no timeout can strand people forever)
derivedDisplayMetadata: two named exits, not one — onEvent and onTimeout must both render as distinct edges, never collapsed into a single 'next'
wait.accessibilityLabelContract: Two edges announce distinctly: 'if {until} happens' and 'after {timeout.after}, because {timeout.reason}'. windowExtendsOnEngagement, when true, is announced explicitly ('this window extends on engagement') since it changes what 'timeout' means operationally.

outcome.presentIn: 1 node total (RET category) — the rarest node kind in the library, present but not statistically meaningful as a design target on its own
derivedDisplayMetadata: renders like an action node with an explicit secondary 'means' field — the one node kind with a true label+detail split at this level
outcome.accessibilityLabelContract: Accessible name = state; means read as supporting detail, same pattern as an exit node.

exit.presentIn: 433 nodes, present in 239/255 journeys (16 self-contained + 209 mixed-termination journeys, per journey-manifest.json's primaryStructure)
requiredData: reEntry (detail — always present, even when terminal=true, explaining WHY no re-entry)
invalidStates: reEntry is empty (validator rejects — err exit_no_reentry)
derivedDisplayMetadata: terminal=true is the rare case (5/433 exits, 5/255 journeys) and is the only one worth a visual badge — flagging all 433 would be noise, per canonical-view.ts's own comment
exit.accessibilityLabelContract: Accessible name = state. reEntry always announces as supporting detail. terminal=true additionally announces 'this state does not allow re-entry' as a distinct qualifier, not folded into the headline.

handoff.presentIn: 500 nodes, 227/255 journeys hand off to another canonical journey, 68/255 to an external:-prefixed pending lifecycle
requiredData: to (a canonical journey id OR an external:<lifecycle> name)
carries (>=1 item recommended — validator warns, does not reject, on empty carries)
invalidStates: to points at a non-existent canonical journey (validator rejects — err handoff_unresolved)
to points at the journey's own id (validator rejects — err handoff_self)
to points at a MERGED id (validator rejects — err handoff_to_merged)
derivedDisplayMetadata: three distinct target kinds, never collapsed into one link style: (1) another live canonical journey — resolvable, addressable, should link; (2) external:<name> — a named but not-yet-defined destination (18 distinct names across 68 journeys) — must render as a clearly PENDING state, not a broken link and not a live one; (3) [not possible per validator] a merged id — structurally forbidden
handoff.accessibilityLabelContract: For a resolvable handoff: accessible name = 'hands off to {target journey name}, when {on}'. For a pending external target: accessible name = 'hands off to a lifecycle not yet defined ({name}), when {on}' — the pending state must be announced, not silently treated as equivalent to a real link. carries items announce as 'carries: {item}'; suppresses items as 'stops: {item}'.

forward.description: trigger.next, action.next, outcome.next — the default single successor.

contract.label: branch.label (short)
contract.navigationBehavior: direct, same-journey, exactly one arm taken at runtime

wait-event.description: wait.onEvent — the arm taken if the awaited event arrives first.

contract.label: on event
contract.navigationBehavior: direct, same-journey, mutually exclusive with wait-timeout

wait-timeout.description: wait.onTimeout — the arm taken if the timeout elapses first.

contract.label: on timeout
contract.navigationBehavior: direct, same-journey, mutually exclusive with wait-event

backward.description: Any of the above whose target sits earlier in the journey's own BFS reading order than its source. Present in 125/255 journeys; forms a true cycle (requires a traversal guard) in 33 of those — see journey-layout-risks.json.

contract.label: inherited
contract.navigationBehavior: same-journey, but the reading direction reverses — must render distinctly (e.g. an upward arrow / back-reference), never as a plain forward line

cross-journey-handoff.description: handoff.to naming another live canonical journey. Present in 227/255 journeys.

contract.navigationBehavior: leaves the current journey view; should be an addressable link to the target journey's own detail page

external.description: handoff.to starting with external:. Present in 68/255 journeys, 18 distinct pending lifecycle names (see EXTERNAL_TARGETS in src/canonical/index.ts).

contract.target: an external:<lifecycle> name, not a resolvable journey
contract.navigationBehavior: must NOT render as a live link — a later category has not yet defined this destination; render as a named, non-clickable pending state

crossFamilyInvariants: Every node kind's edges are named per its own family above — a renderer must not infer edge semantics from shape alone (e.g. a wait node's two edges are never interchangeable with a condition's branches, even though both are 'more than one outgoing edge').

A handoff edge to a MERGED id can never occur in valid data (validator-enforced) — a renderer does not need to handle that case defensively, but a production validator should still assert it stays true.
outcome is real but appears once in the whole library — a renderer must support the node family for correctness, but should not be designed as if it were common.
